sentences.text: Megadontosuchus is distinguished by a robust snout, very large teeth, and large openings on the top of its skull.
Fossils of this animal have been found at Monte Duello in the province of Verona.
The genus Megadontosuchus was first erected by paleontologist Charles C. Mook in 1955.
The species Megadontosuchus arduini was originally named in 1880 under the genus Crocodilius.
A lectotype for Megadontosuchus was not proposed until 2007.
Megadontosuchus is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodile traditionally classified within the subfamily Tomistominae.
This animal lived during the middle Eocene in Italy.
Megadontosuchus lived between 41.03 and 37.71 million years ago during the Bartonian stage.
